submission.natural_language_explanation: L4/H4 is a rare-word copy head: its attention lands almost entirely (weight about 1) on one distinctive piece - in the peaks the word-initial piece - of an already-read rare or unfamiliar word (a personal or place name such as Kollamaunachor, Kljuykov, Schulz, Halvorsen or Strommens, a technical or foreign term such as kuzushiji, katakana or YOCTO, or a low-frequency form such as 'teturned'), and its OV projects that piece's identity straight back into the residual stream, so the write is large exactly when the copied piece is rare. Predict active (peak 1.4-2.5 of the 2.55 max, most often on a sentence-final period, newline, bracket or comma once the rare word is upstream) for passages of two or more sentences that contain such a word, and inactive (0.06-0.3) for text before the rare word appears, for a single short sentence even when it contains a rare name, and for passages of only common vocabulary, where it stays on the passage's first token or copies an ordinary content piece for at most 0.9-1.3.
